english.title: Identifying sex offence complainant in broadcast
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) during the lifetime of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) when **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) had been accused of an offence of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..) and being the

(A)_[body corporate in providing a programme, namely **(..SPECIFY PROGRAMME..),]_
(B)_[person having functions in relation to **(..SPECIFY PROGRAMME..) corresponding to those of an editor of a newspaper]_

included in the programme a matter, namely **(..SPECIFY MATTER..) likely to lead members of the public to identify **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) as the person against whom the offence was alleged to have been committed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(2) and 5(1) of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
during the lifetime of the victim
when a person had been accused of a sexual offence
being the body corporate in providing programme or
person having function in relation to a programme corresponding to that of editor of a newspaper
included in the programme matter likely to lead members of public
to identify the victim

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required for a prosecution.
(ii) See the list of relevant sexual offences to which this offence applies..
(iii) See also offence wordings: H4322 and H4324 which relate to similar offences in other publications and for broadcasting such information.
(iv) See also offence wordings: H4314, H4320 and H4322 which relate to complainants in sex offences where no person has yet been accused.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
